[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Solve the **bracket** and **multiplication** first: (38 + 21) × 2 = 59 × 2 = 118.

Rewrite the expression: 67 + 89 − 53 + 118 − 96.

Group the terms: (67 + 89 + 118) − (53 + 96) = 274 − 149 = 125.

**∴ The correct answer is 125.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

67 + 89 − 53 + (38 + 21) × 2 − 96

Applying the **BODMAS rule** (Brackets, Orders, Division, Multiplication, Addition, Subtraction):

**Step 1:** Solve the **bracket** (B).

⇒ 67 + 89 − 53 + 59 × 2 − 96

**Step 2:** Perform **multiplication** (M).

⇒ 67 + 89 − 53 + 118 − 96

**Step 3:** Perform **addition** and **subtraction** (A and S) from **left to right**.

⇒ 156 − 53 + 118 − 96

⇒ 103 + 118 − 96

⇒ 221 − 96

⇒ 125

**∴ The correct answer is 125.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

BODMAS Rule

It is the standard order of operations used to solve mathematical expressions: **Brackets** first, then **Orders** (exponents/roots), followed by **Division** and **Multiplication** (from left to right), and finally **Addition** and **Subtraction** (from left to right).

Associative Property

While solving only **addition** and **subtraction**, the terms can be grouped together (e.g., all positives together and all negatives together) to simplify the calculation process.

questions.question: 96 + (19 of 2) - 38 + 42 ÷ 6 + 28 - 16 = ?
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Solve **(19 of 2) = 38** and **42 ÷ 6 = 7**.

The expression becomes: **96 + 38 − 38 + 7 + 28 − 16**.

Notice that **+38** and **−38** cancel each other out directly.

Remaining: **96 + 7 + 28 − 16 = 115**.

**∴ The correct answer is 115.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:** 96 + (19 of 2) − 38 + 42 ÷ 6 + 28 − 16

Follow **VBODMAS** rule: Vinculum, Bracket, Of, Division, Multiplication, Addition, Subtraction.

⇒ 96 + (**19 × 2**) − 38 + 42 ÷ 6 + 28 − 16

⇒ 96 + **38** − 38 + (**42 ÷ 6**) + 28 − 16

⇒ 96 + 38 − 38 + **7** + 28 − 16

⇒ (96 + 38 + 7 + 28) − (38 + 16)

⇒ **169 − 54**

⇒ **115**

**∴ The correct answer is 115.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

VBODMAS Rule

This acronym helps remember the order of operations: **Vinculum** (Bar), **Brackets** ((), {}, []), **Of**, **Division** (÷), **Multiplication** (×), **Addition** (+), and **Subtraction** (−).

Precedence of 'Of'

In mathematical expressions, the **'Of'** operator is equivalent to multiplication but must be performed **before** division and general multiplication.

Comparing Rational Numbers

To compare fractions, either convert them to **decimals** or bring them to a **common denominator** by finding the **LCM** of denominators.

Mixed Fraction Conversion

Density Property

Between any two **rational numbers**, there are infinitely many rational numbers that can be found by taking their average or interpolating between them.

questions.question: If X=sqrt{169}times sqrt{121}+sqrt{64}, then what is the value of 2x?
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Directly calculate the **square roots**: √169 = 13, √121 = 11, and √64 = 8.

Apply the calculation: **X** = (13 × 11) + 8 = 143 + 8 = 151.

Find the required value: **2X** = 2 × 151 = 302.

**∴ The correct answer is 302.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

X = √169 × √121 + √64

**Method Used:**

Apply the **BODMAS** rule and **Square Root** simplification.

**Calculations:**

⇒ X = 13 × 11 + 8

⇒ X = 143 + 8

⇒ X = 151

⇒ 2X = 2 × 151

⇒ 2X = 302

**∴ The correct answer is 302.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

BODMAS Rule

It stands for **Brackets, Orders (powers/roots), Division, Multiplication, Addition, and Subtraction**. Operations must be performed in this specific sequence.

Perfect Squares

Squares of numbers from 11 to 15: 11² = 121, 12² = 144, 13² = 169, 14² = 196, 15² = 225.

Multiplication Trick

To multiply any two-digit number by 11, add the two digits and place the sum in between them (e.g., 13 × 11 → 1, (1+3), 3 → 143).

questions.question: The perimeter of a square is 40 cm. What is the side (in cm) of the square?
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

For a **square**, the **Perimeter** is four times its **Side**.

Side = **Perimeter** ÷ 4

Side = 40 ÷ 4 = 10 cm

**∴ The correct answer is 10 cm.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

**Perimeter** of the square = 40 cm

**Formula Used:**

**Perimeter** of a square = 4 × Side (a)

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/480f1603e9ba240e617242cef5cc57a7d3ee269a7a1bfac568863b8f98656db8.png] 

**Calculations:**

⇒ Let the side of the **square** be **a** cm.

⇒ 4 × a = 40

⇒ a = 40 ÷ 4

⇒ a = 10 cm

**∴ The correct answer is 10 cm.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Area of Square

The total surface area covered by the square is **Area** = Side × Side = a².

Diagonal of Square

The length of the diagonal connecting two opposite vertices is **Diagonal** = a√2.

Properties of Square

In a **square**, all four sides are equal, and each interior angle is exactly 90°.

questions.question: The length and breadth of a rectangle is 9 cm and 4 cm respectively. What is the area (in square cm) of the rectangle?

⇒ **Area** = 9 × 4 = 36 cm²

**∴ The correct answer is 36 cm².**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

**Length** of the rectangle = 9 cm

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/06b27d8b9a97a990ddb0dab7d6076ee9b736a302156f1d943c59b590e2d0c6a5.png] 

**Formula Used:**

**Area** = **Length** × **Breadth**

**Calculations:**

Perimeter of a Rectangle

The total boundary length is given by **Perimeter** = 2 × (length + breadth).

Diagonal of a Rectangle

The distance between opposite vertices is **Diagonal** = √(length² + breadth²).

Properties of a Rectangle

All **interior angles** are 90°, opposite sides are **equal and parallel**, and diagonals **bisect each other**.

questions.question: Which of the following number is divisible by both 4 and 9?
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Check **divisibility of 4**: Last two digits must be divisible by 4.

Check **divisibility of 9**: Sum of all digits must be divisible by 9.

Option 1: 4170 → 70 is not divisible by 4.

Option 2: 4128 → Sum of digits (4+1+2+8 = 15) is not divisible by 9.

Option 3: 4092 → Sum of digits (4+0+9+2 = 15) is not divisible by 9.

Option 4: 4032 → 32 ÷ 4 = 8 and Sum (4+0+3+2 = 9) is divisible by 9.

**∴ The correct answer is 4032.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:** Numbers 4170, 4128, 4092, 4032.

**Rules Applied:** **Divisibility rule of 4** (last two digits) and **Divisibility rule of 9** (sum of digits).

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/3dd18b2f756b83e0ebaf29fe11feef3bacecec7cf39aee10df17e2bda735d2a4.png] 

⇒ Check 4170: Last two digits 70 ÷ 4 = 17.5 (Not divisible). Sum = 4+1+7+0 = 12 (Not divisible by 9).

⇒ Check 4128: Last two digits 28 ÷ 4 = 7 (Divisible). Sum = 4+1+2+8 = 15 (Not divisible by 9).

⇒ Check 4092: Last two digits 92 ÷ 4 = 23 (Divisible). Sum = 4+0+9+2 = 15 (Not divisible by 9).

⇒ Check 4032: Last two digits 32 ÷ 4 = 8 (Divisible). Sum = 4+0+3+2 = 9 (Divisible by 9).

**∴ The correct answer is 4032.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Divisibility Rule of 3

A number is divisible by 3 if the **sum of its digits** is a multiple of 3.

Divisibility Rule of 8

A number is divisible by 8 if the **last three digits** of the number are divisible by 8.

Divisibility Rule of 6

A number is divisible by 6 if it is **divisible by both 2 and 3** (i.e., it is an even number and its digit sum is divisible by 3).

Divisibility Rule of 11

The difference between the sum of digits at **odd places** and the sum of digits at **even places** must be 0 or a multiple of 11.

questions.question: sqrt{1156} + sqrt{0.36} + sqrt{0.0025} = ?
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

√1156 = 34 (since 30² = 900 and 40² = 1600)

√0.36 = 0.6 (6² = 36, half the decimal places)

√0.0025 = 0.05 (5² = 25, half the decimal places)

Total Sum = 34 + 0.6 + 0.05 = 34.65

**∴ The correct answer is 34.65.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given Expression:** √1156 + √0.36 + √0.0025

Using **Fractional Conversion** for decimal terms:

⇒ √1156 = 34

⇒ √0.36 = √(36 ÷ 100) = 6 ÷ 10 = 0.6

⇒ √0.0025 = √(25 ÷ 10000) = 5 ÷ 100 = 0.05

⇒ **Required Value** = 34 + 0.6 + 0.05

⇒ **Sum** = 34.65

**∴ The correct answer is 34.65.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Square Root of Decimals

When calculating the **square root** of a decimal, if the number has 2n decimal places, the result will have n decimal places.

Perfect Square Identification

A **perfect square** cannot end with the digits 2, 3, 7, or 8. Numbers ending in 6 will have square roots ending in either 4 or 6.

Squares Ending in 5

For any number (n5)², the result is always [n × (n+1)] followed by 25. Example: 35² = (3 × 4)25 = 1225.

questions.question: What is the smallest 4-digit number that is divisible by 36?
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

A number divisible by **36** must be divisible by both **4** and **9** (**36 = 4 × 9**).

Check the **divisibility rule of 9** (sum of digits) for the options:

(1) 1036: 1+0+3+6 = 10 | (2) **1008**: 1+0+0+8 = **9** | (3) 1016: 1+0+1+6 = 8 | (4) 1028: 1+0+2+8 = 11.

Only **1008** is divisible by **9** and its last two digits (**08**) are divisible by **4**.

**∴ The correct answer is 1008.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Smallest **4-digit number** = **1000**

Divisor = **36**

**Method:**

Divide the smallest **4-digit number** by **36** to find the **remainder**, then adjust to find the next multiple.

**Calculations:**

⇒ **1000 ÷ 36**

⇒ **36 × 27 = 972**

⇒ **Remainder = 1000 − 972 = 28**

⇒ To find the next multiple, add (**Divisor − Remainder**) to the number.

⇒ **Adjustment = 36 − 28 = 8**

⇒ **Smallest 4-digit multiple = 1000 + 8 = 1008**

**∴ The correct answer is 1008.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Divisibility Rule of 9

A number is divisible by **9** if the **sum of its digits** is a multiple of **9**.

Divisibility Rule of 4

A number is divisible by **4** if its **last two digits** are divisible by **4** or are both zero.

Smallest n-digit Multiple

Smallest multiple = **Smallest n-digit number + (Divisor − Remainder)**, where the remainder comes from dividing the smallest n-digit number by the divisor.

questions.question: What is the smallest number which when increased by 17 is exactly divisible by 5, 6 and 8?
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

The **smallest number** is obtained by subtracting the increment from the **LCM** of the given divisors.

**LCM** of 5, 6, and 8 ⇒ 120.

Required number = **LCM** − **17**.

Number = 120 − 17 = **103**.

**∴ The correct answer is 103.**

questions.question: What is the largest 2 digit number which is exactly divisible by both 8 and 7?
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Find the **LCM** of 8 and 7 to get the smallest number divisible by both.

**LCM(8, 7)** = 8 × 7 = **56** (since they are co-prime).

The next multiple is 56 × 2 = **112**, which is a 3-digit number.

Thus, the **largest 2-digit number** divisible by both is 56.

**∴ The correct answer is 56.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Divisors = **8** and **7**

Target = **Largest 2-digit number** exactly divisible by both.

**Formula Used:**

A number divisible by multiple numbers is also divisible by their **Least Common Multiple (LCM)**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/1c4f6a693ccb6aa7096bb8568dd21fa4934519f4b81a3ecf1fddcb502bf52c72.png] 

**Calculations:**

⇒ Step 1: Calculate the **LCM** of 8 and 7.

⇒ Prime factorization of 8 = 2 × 2 × 2

⇒ Prime factorization of 7 = 7

⇒ **LCM(8, 7)** = 2³ × 7 = 56

⇒ Step 2: List the multiples of 56 to find the **largest 2-digit** one.

⇒ 56 × 1 = **56**

⇒ 56 × 2 = **112**

⇒ Since 112 is a **3-digit number** and the maximum 2-digit number is 99, 112 is excluded.

⇒ The largest 2-digit multiple is therefore 56.

**∴ The correct answer is 56.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Least Common Multiple (LCM)

The smallest positive integer that is a multiple of two or more numbers. For **co-prime** numbers (numbers with HCF = 1), the LCM is always the **product** of the numbers.

Co-prime Numbers Property

If **a** and **b** are co-prime, then any number divisible by both **a** and **b** must also be divisible by their product (**a × b**).

Divisibility Rule of 8 and 7

A number is divisible by 8 if its last three digits are divisible by 8. For 7, subtract twice the last digit from the remaining number; if the result is divisible by 7, the original number is too.

questions.question: A is (1/5) of B. A is how much percent less than B?
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Ratio of **A : B = 1 : 5**

Value of **B** is 5 units and **A** is 1 unit.

Difference = 5 − 1 = **4 units**.

Percentage less = (Difference ÷ Value of B) × 100 = (4 ÷ 5) × 100 = **80%**.

**∴ The correct answer is 80 percent.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

**A** = (1/5) × **B**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ab3a73843e31fe5a5b70cbb99cff93a3637d059363e34e396246335a9791938e.png] 

**Calculation:**

⇒ **A / B = 1 / 5**

⇒ Let **B** = 5x and **A** = 1x

⇒ **Difference** = B − A = 5x − 1x = 4x

⇒ **Percentage less** = (Difference ÷ B) × 100

⇒ Percentage less = (4x ÷ 5x) × 100

⇒ Percentage less = (4 ÷ 5) × 100 = **80%**

**∴ The correct answer is 80 percent.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Percentage Decrease Formula

Percentage Less = [(Reference Value − Target Value) ÷ Reference Value] × 100.

Fraction to Percentage Conversion

To convert any fraction x/y into percentage, multiply the fraction by 100 (e.g., 1/5 × 100 = 20%).

Complementary Percentages

If A is 20% of B, then A is (100% − 20%) = 80% less than B.

questions.question: Selling price and cost price of an article is Rs. 920 and Rs. 800 respectively. What is the profit percentage?
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

**Profit** = 920 − 800 = ₹120

**Profit %** = (Profit ÷ CP) × 100

**Profit %** = (120 ÷ 800) × 100 = 15%

**∴ The correct answer is 15%.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

**Cost Price (CP)** of the article = ₹800

**Selling Price (SP)** of the article = ₹920

**Formula Used:**

Profit = **Selling Price (SP)** − **Cost Price (CP)**

Profit Percentage = (Profit ÷ **Cost Price (CP)**) × 100

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4acf4ce2b1b33f3b7fd38143edf1eda9ac48e5d7c62b92e9d4c2fc04774cf6bb.png] 

**Calculations:**

⇒ **Profit** = 920 − 800

⇒ **Profit** = ₹120

⇒ **Profit Percentage** = (120 ÷ 800) × 100

⇒ **Profit Percentage** = (12 ÷ 80) × 100

⇒ **Profit Percentage** = (3 ÷ 20) × 100

⇒ **Profit Percentage** = 3 × 5 = 15%

**∴ The correct answer is 15%.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Loss Percentage

When the **Cost Price (CP)** is greater than the **Selling Price (SP)**, a loss occurs. Loss% = [(CP − SP) ÷ CP] × 100.

Marked Price and Discount

**Marked Price (MP)** is the price printed on an item. **Discount** is always calculated on the MP. SP = MP − Discount.

Relation between CP and SP

SP = CP × [(100 + Profit%) ÷ 100] for profit cases, and SP = CP × [(100 − Loss%) ÷ 100] for loss cases.

questions.question: A person sells an article at the loss of 40 percent. Cost price and selling price both are decreased by 50 percent. What will be the new loss percentage?
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

If both the **Cost Price (CP)** and **Selling Price (SP)** are multiplied or divided by the same factor (or decreased/increased by the same percentage), the **ratio** between them remains unchanged.

Since both CP and SP are decreased by **50%**, they are both halved, keeping the ratio **CP : SP** constant.

Original ratio ⇒ CP : SP = 100 : 60 (for a 40% loss).

New ratio ⇒ 50 : 30 = 100 : 60.

Because the ratio is unchanged, the **loss percentage** remains **40%**.

**∴ The correct answer is 40 percent.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:** Initial Loss % = 40%, Reduction in CP and SP = 50%.

**Formula Used:** Loss % = [(CP − SP) ÷ CP] × 100

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f70c014c6d5a6c9c1260d30a7b56d50a4e6575be8a9659d96a3012114beb0305.png] 

⇒ Let the initial **Cost Price (CP₁)** = 100.

⇒ Initial **Selling Price (SP₁)** = CP₁ − 40% of CP₁ = 100 − 40 = 60.

⇒ New **Cost Price (CP₂)** = 100 − 50% of 100 = 50.

⇒ New **Selling Price (SP₂)** = 60 − 50% of 60 = 30.

⇒ New **Loss Amount** = CP₂ − SP₂ = 50 − 30 = 20.

⇒ New **Loss Percentage** = (New Loss ÷ CP₂) × 100

⇒ New **Loss Percentage** = (20 ÷ 50) × 100 = 40%.

**∴ The correct answer is 40 percent.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Profit and Loss % Invariance

The profit or loss percentage remains unchanged if both the Cost Price and Selling Price are multiplied or divided by the same non-zero constant (constant ratio).

Loss Percentage Formula

Loss % is calculated as (Loss ÷ CP) × 100. It measures the loss relative to the initial investment (CP).

Successive Changes in CP and SP

If CP changes by x% and SP changes by y%, the new profit/loss % must be calculated using the new values: New % = [(SP × (1+y/100) − CP × (1+x/100)) ÷ (CP × (1+x/100))] × 100.

questions.question: P got 20 percent less marks than Q. R got 50 percent less marks than Q. If sum of P, R and Q marks is 2300, then what is the difference between the marks of Q and R?
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Ratio of marks **P : Q : R** = 80 : 100 : 50 = **8 : 10 : 5**

Total sum of ratio units = 8 + 10 + 5 = **23 units**

Given 23 units = **2300** → 1 unit = **100**

Difference between **Q** and **R** = 10 − 5 = **5 units**

Required difference = 5 × 100 = **500**

**∴ The correct answer is 500.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/cc816170891d7e90e1e7346abede4252995e125a21451946ed57df163d069ebb.png] 

**Given:**

Marks of **P** = **Q** − 20% of **Q** = 0.8**Q**

Marks of **R** = **Q** − 50% of **Q** = 0.5**Q**

Sum of marks (**P + Q + R**) = **2300**

**Calculations:**

⇒ 0.8**Q** + 1.0**Q** + 0.5**Q** = 2300

⇒ 2.3**Q** = 2300

⇒ **Q** = 2300 ÷ 2.3 = **1000**

⇒ **R** = 0.5 × 1000 = **500**

⇒ Difference = **Q − R** = 1000 − 500 = **500**

**∴ The correct answer is 500.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Percentage to Ratio Conversion

Comparing values by converting percentages to units simplifies calculations significantly in competitive exams.

Percentage Change Formula

Final Value = Initial Value × (100 ± x)/100, where x is the percentage increase or decrease.

Difference between Values

The difference between two quantities can be found directly from their ratio parts without calculating individual values first: Difference = (Diff in parts ÷ Sum of parts) × Total Sum.

questions.question: 25 men can complete a work in 60 days. 15 men will complete 50 percent of the same work in how many days?
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Total work capacity = **25 men** × **60 days** = 1500 units.

Target work (**50% work**) = 1500 ÷ 2 = 750 units.

Days required for **15 men** = 750 ÷ 15 = **50 days**.

**∴ The correct answer is 50 days.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Initial men (M₁) = **25 men**

Initial days (D₁) = **60 days**

Target men (M₂) = **15 men**

Work ratio = W₁ is 1, W₂ is 0.5 (**50 percent**)

**Formula Used:**

(M₁ × D₁) ÷ W₁ = (M₂ × D₂) ÷ W₂

 
 

 **Person**
 **Days**
 **Total Work**
 **Efficiency**
 
 

 **25 Men**
 60
 1500
 25
 
 

 **15 Men**
 D₂
 15
 
 

**Calculations:**

⇒ (25 × 60) ÷ 1 = (15 × D₂) ÷ 0.5

⇒ 1500 = 30 × D₂

⇒ D₂ = 1500 ÷ 30

⇒ D₂ = **50 days**

**∴ The correct answer is 50 days.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Chain Rule Formula

Used to solve problems with multiple variables: (M₁×D₁×H₁)/W₁ = (M₂×D₂×H₂)/W₂, where M is men, D is days, H is hours, and W is work.

Work and Efficiency

Efficiency is **inversely proportional** to the time taken to complete the work (Efficiency ∝ 1/Time).

Man-Days Concept

Total work is the product of the number of workers and the time they work (Work = Men × Days).

questions.question: R, M and T work for 4 days, 6 days and 8 days respectively. They get a total amount of Rs. 540 for their work. Ratio of one day work of R, M and T is 1 : 2 : 3 respectively. How much money (in Rs.) does M get?
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Ratio of total work done (and thus **wages**) is Efficiency × Days.

Ratio of shares (R : M : T) = (1 × 4) : (2 × 6) : (3 × 8) = 4 : 12 : 24 = 1 : 3 : 6.

Total units = 1 + 3 + 6 = 10 units → ₹540.

1 unit = ₹54 ∴ M's share = 3 units = 3 × ₹54 = ₹162.

**∴ The correct answer is ₹162.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Time worked by **R** = 4 days, **M** = 6 days, **T** = 8 days.

One day work (Efficiency) ratio **R : M : T** = 1 : 2 : 3.

Total amount distributed = **₹540**.

**Formula Used:**

Individual Wage = (Efficiency × Number of Days worked)

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/7fd120777b781918a9b720aea17a5ac2c2a8c2f6d22ae96a08dc7cded3fbb1c4.png] 

**Calculations:**

⇒ Total work done by R = 1 × 4 = 4 units

⇒ Total work done by M = 2 × 6 = 12 units

⇒ Total work done by T = 3 × 8 = 24 units

⇒ Ratio of shares = 4 : 12 : 24

⇒ Simplify ratio by dividing by 4: 1 : 3 : 6

⇒ Let shares be x, 3x, and 6x

⇒ x + 3x + 6x = 540

⇒ 10x = 540

⇒ x = 54

⇒ Share of M = 3x = 3 × 54 = 162

**∴ The correct answer is ₹162.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Work and Wages Concept

Wages are distributed in the ratio of the total work done by each person. Work Done = Efficiency × Time.

Efficiency and Time Relationship

If work is constant, Efficiency is inversely proportional to Time (E ∝ 1/T). However, for wages, we always use the actual units of work completed.

Ratio Distribution

To find a specific share from a total: Share = (Individual Ratio Part ÷ Sum of Ratio Parts) × Total Amount.

questions.question: The speed of a train is 72 km/hr. Length of the train is 180 metres. In how much time (in seconds) it will cross a platform of length 120 metres?
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Convert **speed** from km/hr to m/s: 72 × (5/18) = 20 m/s.

Total **Distance** = Train length + Platform length = 180 + 120 = 300 m.

**Time taken** = Total Distance ÷ Speed = 300 ÷ 20 = 15 sec.

**∴ The correct answer is 15 sec.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

**Speed of the train** = 72 km/hr

**Length of the train** = 180 m

**Length of the platform** = 120 m

**Formula Used:**

Speed = Distance ÷ Time

To convert km/hr to m/s, multiply by 5/18.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/3225a2cbb73c78d648e157d761b07556f7399d3bfa0eea65f911abe6d6e15e7c.png] 

**Calculations:**

⇒ **Speed** in m/s = 72 × (5/18)

⇒ **Speed** = 4 × 5 = 20 m/s

⇒ **Total Distance** to be covered = Length of train + Length of platform

⇒ **Total Distance** = 180 + 120 = 300 m

⇒ **Time** = Distance ÷ Speed

⇒ **Time** = 300 ÷ 20

⇒ **Time** = 15 sec

**∴ The correct answer is 15 sec.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Unit Conversion

To convert **Speed** from km/hr to m/s, multiply by 5/18. To convert from m/s to km/hr, multiply by 18/5.

Crossing Stationary Objects

When a **train** crosses a stationary object with length (like a **bridge** or **platform**), the total distance is (Length of train + Length of object). For a point object (like a **pole**), distance equals the length of the train.

Relative Speed

When two objects move in the **same direction**, relative speed is (S₁ − S₂). In **opposite directions**, it is (S₁ + S₂).

questions.question: A train moving with the speed of 60 km/hr crosses a platform in 10 minutes. Length of the train and the platform is same. What is the length (in metres) of the platform?
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Total distance covered in 10 minutes at 60 km/hr = 60 × (10/60) = 10 km.

Total distance = 10,000 m.

Since the **Length** of the **Train** and the **Platform** are equal:

2 × **Platform Length** = 10,000 m.

**Platform Length** = 10,000 ÷ 2 = 5,000 m.

**∴ The correct answer is 5000 m.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

**Speed** of **Train** = 60 km/hr

**Time** taken to cross = 10 minutes

**Length** of **Train** (Lₜ) = **Length** of **Platform** (Lₚ)

**Formula Used:**

Distance = Speed × Time

Total Distance = Lₜ + Lₚ

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f554cbab2824461e6c82b053231a6b9e3194c597e072b8eef2928c0cef1615d9.png] 

**Calculations:**

⇒ Let Lₜ = Lₚ = L

⇒ Total Distance = L + L = 2L

⇒ Speed in m/s = 60 × (5/18) = 50/3 m/s

⇒ Time in seconds = 10 × 60 = 600 s

⇒ Distance = (50/3) × 600

⇒ 2L = 50 × 200

⇒ 2L = 10,000

⇒ L = 5,000 m

**∴ The correct answer is 5000 m.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Unit Conversion

To convert **speed** from km/hr to m/s, multiply by 5/18. To convert from m/s to km/hr, multiply by 18/5.

Relative Distance

When a **train** crosses a stationary object of length 'P', the total distance covered is (Length of train + P). If it crosses a point object (pole/man), the distance is just the Length of the train.

Time, Speed, and Distance

The fundamental relation is Distance = Speed × Time. Ensure all variables are in consistent units (e.g., metres and seconds, or km and hours) before calculating.
